question_text: A 67-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of the sudden onset of severe substernal chest pain at rest. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and alcohol use disorder. He is diaphoretic and appears anxious. The lungs are clear to auscultation. An ECG shows ST-segment elevations in leads I, aVL, V5, and V6. One hour later, he develops dyspnea and a productive cough with frothy sputum. Which of the following best describes the most likely underlying pathophysiology of this patient's dyspnea?
